canonical_question: Does the cited ~60% efficiency improvement refer to a specific combined cycle configuration, and how does this compare to the baseline conventional cycle?

question_variants.question: Does the cited ~60% efficiency improvement refer to a specific combined cycle configuration, and how does this compare to the baseline conventional cycle?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that the technology can enhance net efficiency up to approximately 60% for the system compared to a conventional thermal power cycle, but does not specify the exact configuration of the combined cycle or the baseline efficiency value.

answers.answer: The text mentions the potential to enhance net up to ~60% efficiency for the system as compared to a conventional thermal power cycle, but provides no further details on the specific combined cycle configuration or the baseline value.
answers.measurement_outcome: Potential net efficiency enhancement up to ~60%.
answers.boundary_limitation: No specific cycle configuration or baseline defined.
evidence_spans: Lu et al. [14] reported the effect of Al content on the oxidation behavior of Y/Hf-doped Al x CoCrFeNi ( x = 0.7, 1, 1.3) high-entropy alloys. Al 0.7 CoCrFeNi showed the lowest oxidation resistance owing to the formation of an outer spinel layer with an inner Al 2 O 3 layer, followed by AlCoCrFeNi due to the formation of protective Al 2 O 3 scale and Al 1.3 CoCrFeNi exhibiting the highest resistance to oxidation.
